batchName: Middle Republic: The First Punic War (264-241 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Middle Republic: The First Punic War (264-241 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What was the rostrum on a Roman warship?
options: A bronze ram at the waterline
questions.explanation: It was used to smash enemy hulls, and could weigh up to 270 kg (600 lb).
questions.sourceQuote: At the waterline sat a bronze ram (*rostrum*) weighing up to 270 kg (600 lb), used for smashing enemy hulls.

questions.question: After the war Sicily became Rome’s first provincia. What was that?
options: An overseas territory run by a Roman governor
An allied city with its own king
questions.explanation: Sicily also became a vital source of grain for Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: Sicily became Rome's first province (*provincia*), an overseas territory run by a Roman governor

questions.question: Why is the war called “Punic”?
options: From Punici, the Romans’ name for the Carthaginians
From a Sicilian city called Punicum
From the name of a Carthaginian king
questions.explanation: Punici means Phoenicians, the ancestors of the Carthaginians.
questions.sourceQuote: Romans called the Carthaginians *Punici*, meaning Phoenicians, after their ancestors.

questions.question: In 264 BC the deadlocked Senate passed the question of war to the comitia. What was it?
questions.explanation: One of the consuls urged war and promised rich plunder; the people voted yes.
questions.sourceQuote: so the question went to the popular assembly (*comitia*).

questions.question: What did a consul promise the voters to win support for war in 264 BC?
options: Land in Sicily for every voter
questions.explanation: Many Romans disliked aiding the Mamertines, but the promise of plunder helped carry the vote.

questions.question: Before 260 BC, how did Rome get warships?
options: It borrowed small squadrons from its allies (socii)
It had a large navy of its own
questions.explanation: In 260 BC it began building its own fleet, copying a shipwrecked Carthaginian warship.
questions.sourceQuote: having always borrowed small squadrons from its allies (*socii*).

questions.question: About how many men were in each of the two legiones that crossed to Sicily in 264 BC?
questions.explanation: By 263 BC there were 40,000 Romans on the island.
questions.sourceQuote: two legions (*legiones*), Roman army units of about 4,500 men each

questions.question: What was the triumphus that Catulus celebrated?
options: A naval review at the coast
A feast for the whole army
questions.explanation: Catulus’s fleet had won the final battle of the war at the Aegates Islands.
questions.sourceQuote: celebrated a triumph (*triumphus*), a victory parade through Rome.
